problem: Digest quotes Wolf's 1989 speech ('revolutionary renewal'); modern text. ('Wende' as a term and 'We are the people' as a famous slogan can stay.)

fix.digest: Speaking to the largest demonstration in GDR history, Wolf said the revolution had first freed language itself: stiff official German was giving way to living speech. She disliked the regime's word 'Wende', preferring to speak of a revolutionary renewal from below, and asked people to imagine a socialism no one would want to flee. She warned against officials changing sides too nimbly and called 'We are the people' the most important sentence of the autumn.

fix.headline: A British cable relays a casualty figure from a Chinese contact
fix.digest: Donald cabled London with an account he had received from a Chinese contact describing how the square and surrounding streets were cleared and putting the dead at a minimum of ten thousand. He reported it as information received, not as his own observation. The Chinese government spoke of about 200–300 dead including soldiers, and the US embassy's later reconstruction put civilian deaths probably below three thousand; each figure is given here as its source gave it.
